subject: Physics
topic: Dynamics and Equilibrium of Rigid Bodies (Torque)
subtopic: Newton's Laws, Torque (Moment of Force), Couples & Rotational Equilibrium
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Physics Mechanics Unit 1: Forces, Torque, and Equilibrium of a Rigid Body (ឌីណាមិច និងលំនឹងនៃអង្គធាតុរឹង). The torque (moment of force, ម៉ូម៉ង់នៃកម្លាំង) about an axis O is M_O(F) = tau = F * d = r F sin(theta), where d = r sin(theta) is the lever arm (ដៃឃ្នាស់). A rigid body is in complete mechanical equilibrium if and only if both conditions hold: (1) translational equilibrium sum F = 0, and (2) rotational equilibrium sum M_O = 0.

source.section: Newton's Laws, Torque (Moment of Force), Couples & Rotational Equilibrium

metadata.topic_khmer: ឌីណាមិច និងលំនឹងនៃអង្គធាតុរឹង (ម៉ូម៉ង់កម្លាំង)
metadata.subtopic_khmer: ច្បាប់ញូតុន ម៉ូម៉ង់នៃកម្លាំង ម៉ូម៉ង់នៃគូកម្លាំង និងលក្ខខណ្ឌលំនឹងអង្គធាតុរឹង
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាម៉ូម៉ង់នៃកម្លាំងធៀបនឹងអ័ក្សរង្វិល ដៃឃ្នាស់ ម៉ូម៉ង់នៃគូកម្លាំង ទីប្រជុំទម្ងន់ និងលក្ខខណ្ឌលំនឹងទាំងពីរនៃអង្គធាតុរឹង។
metadata.starter_problem: \tau = F \cdot d = rF\sin\theta, \quad r = 0.4\text{ m}, \; F = 50\text{ N}, \; \theta = 30^\circ
learning_objectives: Calculate the lever arm d = r sin(theta) and torque tau = rF sin(theta) in N*m
Apply the two conditions of static equilibrium (sum F = 0 and sum tau = 0) to beams, levers, and ladders

concepts.title: Torque & Lever Arm (ម៉ូម៉ង់នៃកម្លាំង និងដៃឃ្នាស់)
concepts.summary: Measuring the turning effect of a force about a pivot.
concepts.body: The torque of force F about pivot O is tau = F * d = r F sin(theta), where r is the distance from O to the point of application and theta is the angle between r and F. A force whose line of action passes through the pivot (d = 0) produces zero torque.

concepts.title: Conditions of Equilibrium of a Rigid Body (លក្ខខណ្ឌលំនឹងនៃអង្គធាតុរឹង)
concepts.summary: Zero net force (sum F = 0) and zero net torque (sum tau = 0).
concepts.body: For a rigid body to remain at rest: (1) sum F_x = 0 and sum F_y = 0 (no linear acceleration), and (2) sum tau_counterclockwise = sum tau_clockwise about any chosen pivot O.

khmer_terms.Dynamics and Equilibrium of Rigid Bodies: ឌីណាមិច និងលំនឹងនៃអង្គធាតុរឹង (ម៉ូម៉ង់កម្លាំង)
khmer_terms.Newton's Laws, Torque (Moment of Force),: ច្បាប់ញូតុន ម៉ូម៉ង់នៃកម្លាំង ម៉ូម៉ង់នៃគូកម្លាំង និងលក្ខខណ្ឌលំនឹងអង្គធាតុរឹង
khmer_terms.rigid body: អង្គធាតុរឹង
khmer_terms.torque (moment of force): ម៉ូម៉ង់នៃកម្លាំង
khmer_terms.axis of rotation: អ័ក្សរង្វិល
khmer_terms.rotational equilibrium: លំនឹងរង្វិល
khmer_terms.center of gravity: ទីប្រជុំទម្ងន់

examples.problem: A wrench of length r = 0.40 m is pulled with a force F = 50 N at an angle theta = 30 degrees to the handle. Calculate the torque about the bolt.
solution_steps: Step 1: Lever arm d = r sin(30 deg) = 0.40 * 0.5 = 0.20 m.
Step 2: Torque tau = F * d = 50 * 0.20 = 10 N m.

examples.problem: A uniform massless seesaw is pivoted at its center. A 300 N child sits 2.0 m to the left of the pivot. Where must a 400 N child sit on the right to balance the seesaw?
examples.answer: 1.5 m to the right of the pivot
solution_steps: Step 1: Apply rotational equilibrium: tau_left = tau_right => F_1 d_1 = F_2 d_2.

exercises.prompt: A horizontal beam of weight 200 N and length 4 m is supported at both ends A and B, with a 100 N load placed 1 m from A. Find the upward support forces N_A and N_B.
hints: Take torques about A: N_B(4) = 100(1) + 200(2), then use N_A + N_B = 300 N.

solution_steps: Step 1: Choose a convenient pivot point O (where an unknown force acts, so its torque is zero).
Step 2: Compute perpendicular lever arms d_i = r_i sin(theta_i) and equate clockwise and counterclockwise torques.
Step 3: Use sum F_x = 0 and sum F_y = 0 to find remaining support forces.

common_misconceptions.text: Multiplying force by total rod length r without sin(theta) when the force is applied at an oblique angle.
common_misconceptions.correction: Only the component of force perpendicular to r (F sin theta) produces torque.

teaching_sequence: Review prerequisites and Khmer MoEYS terminology
Introduce core concept and governing formulas
Walk through step-by-step worked examples on the whiteboard
Check student understanding with guided exercises and misconception checks

subject: Physics
topic: Work, Energy, Linear Momentum and Collisions
subtopic: Work-Energy Theorem, Impulse, Conservation of Momentum & Elastic/Inelastic Collisions
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Physics Mechanics Unit 2: Work, Energy, Linear Momentum and Collisions (កម្មន្ត ថាមពល បរិមាណចលនា និងការទង្គិច). Linear momentum is p = mv (kg m/s) and impulse is J = F Delta t = Delta p. In an isolated system (sum F_ext = 0), total linear momentum is conserved: m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 = m_1 v'_1 + m_2 v'_2. In an elastic collision (ទង្គិចស្ទាត់), both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved; in a perfectly inelastic collision (ទង្គិចទន់), the bodies stick together with common velocity v' = (m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2)/(m_1 + m_2).

source.section: Work-Energy Theorem, Impulse, Conservation of Momentum & Elastic/Inelastic Collisions

metadata.topic_khmer: កម្មន្ត ថាមពល បរិមាណចលនា និងការទង្គិច
metadata.subtopic_khmer: ទ្រឹស្តីបទថាមពលស៊ីនេទិច អាំពុលស្យុង ច្បាប់រក្សាបរិមាណចលនា និងការទង្គិច
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាទ្រឹស្តីបទថាមពលស៊ីនេទិច បរិមាណចលនា p = mv អាំពុលស្យុងនៃកម្លាំង ច្បាប់រក្សាបរិមាណចលនា ព្រមទាំងការទង្គិចស្ទាត់ និងទង្គិចទន់។
metadata.starter_problem: m_1 = 2\text{ kg at } v_1 = 6\text{ m/s collides inelastically with } m_2 = 4\text{ kg at rest. Find } v'.
learning_objectives: Apply the Work-Energy Theorem W_net = Delta E_k = (1/2)mv_2^2 - (1/2)mv_1^2
Calculate linear momentum p = mv and impulse F Delta t = m v_2 - m v_1
Solve 1D elastic and perfectly inelastic collision problems using conservation of momentum

concepts.title: Impulse & Conservation of Linear Momentum (អាំពុលស្យុង និងច្បាប់រក្សាបរិមាណចលនា)
concepts.summary: F Delta t = Delta p and m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 = m_1 v'_1 + m_2 v'_2.
concepts.body: Momentum p = mv is a vector. During any short collision or explosion where external forces are negligible compared to internal impact forces, total vector momentum before equals total vector momentum after.

concepts.title: Elastic vs Inelastic Collisions (ការទង្គិចស្ទាត់ និងការទង្គិចទន់)
concepts.summary: Comparing kinetic energy before and after collision.
concepts.body: Momentum is conserved in ALL isolated collisions. Kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic collisions. In a perfectly inelastic collision, the two objects stick together and move at v' = (m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2)/(m_1 + m_2), losing kinetic energy Delta E_k as heat/sound/deformation.

khmer_terms.Work, Energy, Linear Momentum and Collis: កម្មន្ត ថាមពល បរិមាណចលនា និងការទង្គិច
khmer_terms.Work-Energy Theorem, Impulse, Conservati: ទ្រឹស្តីបទថាមពលស៊ីនេទិច អាំពុលស្យុង ច្បាប់រក្សាបរិមាណចលនា និងការទង្គិច
khmer_terms.linear momentum: បរិមាណចលនា p
khmer_terms.impulse: អាំពុលស្យុងនៃកម្លាំង
khmer_terms.conservation of momentum: ច្បាប់រក្សាបរិមាណចលនា
khmer_terms.elastic collision: ការទង្គិចស្ទាត់
khmer_terms.perfectly inelastic collision: ការទង្គិចទន់
khmer_terms.kinetic energy theorem: ទ្រឹស្តីបទថាមពលស៊ីនេទិច

formulas.name: Impulse-Momentum Theorem & Momentum Conservation
formulas.expression: \vec{p} = m\vec{v}, \quad \vec{F}\Delta t = \Delta\vec{p}, \quad m_1\vec{v}_1 + m_2\vec{v}_2 = m_1\vec{v}_1' + m_2\vec{v}_2'

formulas.name: Perfectly Inelastic Collision & Work-Energy Theorem
formulas.expression: v' = \frac{m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2}{m_1 + m_2}, \quad W_{\text{net}} = \Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv_2^2 - \frac{1}{2}mv_1^2

examples.problem: A 2 kg cart moving at v_1 = 6 m/s collides head-on and sticks to a 4 kg cart initially at rest. Find their common final velocity v' and the kinetic energy lost in the collision.
solution_steps: Step 1: By momentum conservation, v' = (m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2)/(m_1 + m_2) = (2*6 + 0)/(2 + 4) = 12/6 = 2 m/s.
Step 3: Kinetic energy lost = 36 - 12 = 24 J.

exercises.prompt: A 0.5 kg ball moving at +10 m/s hits a wall and rebounds at -8 m/s in 0.02 s. Find the magnitude of the impulse and average force exerted by the wall.
hints: Include the sign reversal: Delta p = m(v_2 - v_1) = 0.5(-8 - 10).
solution_steps: Delta p = 0.5 * (-8 - 10) = -9 kg m/s (magnitude 9 N s).
Step 1: Assign a positive axis and attach +/- signs to all velocities.
Step 2: Apply conservation of linear momentum m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 = m_1 v'_1 + m_2 v'_2.
Step 3: Check kinetic energy before and after if asked about elasticity or energy loss.

common_misconceptions.text: Omitting the negative sign when an object rebounds in the opposite direction (computing Delta v = 10 - 8 = 2 instead of -8 - 10 = -18).
common_misconceptions.correction: Velocity and momentum are vectors; reversing direction requires opposite algebraic signs.

teaching_sequence: Review prerequisites and Khmer MoEYS terminology
Introduce core concept and governing formulas
Walk through step-by-step worked examples on the whiteboard
Check student understanding with guided exercises and misconception checks

subject: Physics
subtopic: Coulomb's Law, Superposition of Electric Fields, Potential Energy & Capacitors
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Physics Electricity Unit 1: Electrostatics, Electric Field and Electric Potential (អេឡិចត្រូស្តាទិច ដែនអគ្គិសនី និងប៉ូតង់ស្យែលអគ្គិសនី). Covers quantization and conservation of charge, Coulomb's Law F = k|q_1 q_2|/r^2, electric field vector E = F/q_0 = k|Q|/r^2 (directed away from +Q and toward -Q), work of the electrostatic force W_{AB} = q(V_A - V_B) = q U_{AB} = q E d, and parallel-plate capacitors.

source.section: Coulomb's Law, Superposition of Electric Fields, Potential Energy & Capacitors

metadata.topic_khmer: អេឡិចត្រូស្តាទិច ដែនអគ្គិសនី និងប៉ូតង់ស្យែលអគ្គិសនី
metadata.subtopic_khmer: ច្បាប់គូឡុំ គោលការណ៍តម្រួតដែនអគ្គិសនី កម្មន្តនៃកម្លាំងអគ្គិសនី និងកុងដង់សាទ័រ
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាច្បាប់គូឡុំ ដែនអគ្គិសនីបង្កើតដោយបន្ទុកចំណុច កម្មន្តនៃកម្លាំងអគ្គិសនី ផលសងប៉ូតង់ស្យែល U = Ed និងកុងដង់សាទ័របន្ទះស្រប។
metadata.starter_problem: q_1 = +2\,\mu\text{C}, \; q_2 = -4\,\mu\text{C at } r = 0.3\text{ m. Find Coulomb force } F.
learning_objectives: Calculate Coulomb forces and resultant electric fields using vector superposition
Compute electrostatic work W_{AB} = q U_{AB} = q E d and final speed of charged particles accelerated through voltage U

concepts.title: Coulomb's Law & Electric Field Superposition (ច្បាប់គូឡុំ និងតម្រួតដែនអគ្គិសនី)
concepts.summary: Inverse-square electrostatic force and vector sum E = E_1 + E_2.
concepts.body: Two point charges interact with force F = k|q_1 q_2|/r^2 (k = 9e9 N m^2/C^2). A point charge Q creates electric field E = k|Q|/r^2 radially outward if Q > 0 and inward if Q < 0.

concepts.title: Electric Work & Particle Acceleration in a Voltage U (កម្មន្តអគ្គិសនី និងសំទុះភាគល្អិតផ្ទុកបន្ទុក)
concepts.summary: Using W = qU = Delta E_k to find particle speed.
concepts.body: When a charge q accelerates from rest through a potential difference U, electrostatic work equals kinetic energy gained: |q|U = (1/2)mv^2 => v = sqrt(2|q|U / m).

khmer_terms.Electrostatics, Electric Field and Poten: អេឡិចត្រូស្តាទិច ដែនអគ្គិសនី និងប៉ូតង់ស្យែលអគ្គិសនី
khmer_terms.Coulomb's Law, Superposition of Electric: ច្បាប់គូឡុំ គោលការណ៍តម្រួតដែនអគ្គិសនី កម្មន្តនៃកម្លាំងអគ្គិសនី និងកុងដង់សាទ័រ
khmer_terms.Coulomb's law: ច្បាប់គូឡុំ
khmer_terms.electric field strength: អាំងតង់ស៊ីតេដែនអគ្គិសនី E
khmer_terms.potential difference (voltage): ផលសងប៉ូតង់ស្យែល (តង់ស្យុង U)
khmer_terms.elementary charge: បន្ទុកអគ្គិសនីបឋម e

formulas.name: Coulomb's Law, Point-Charge Field & Electrostatic Work
formulas.expression: F = k\frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2}, \quad E = k\frac{|Q|}{r^2}, \quad W_{AB} = q(V_A - V_B) = qU_{AB} = qEd

examples.problem: Two point charges q_1 = +2\,\mu\text{C} and q_2 = -4\,\mu\text{C} are separated by r = 0.30\text{ m} in air. Find the magnitude and nature of the electrostatic force between them.
solution_steps: Step 1: Convert charges: |q_1| = 2e-6 C, |q_2| = 4e-6 C.
Step 2: F = (9e9 * 2e-6 * 4e-6) / (0.30)^2 = 0.072 / 0.09 = 0.80 N (attractive since opposite signs).

exercises.prompt: Find the electric field strength E at a distance r = 0.20 m from a point charge Q = +4 nC.
hints: Use E = k|Q|/r^2 with Q = 4 x 10^{-9} C.

solution_steps: Step 1: Use absolute values |q| inside F and E formulas to find magnitudes.
Step 2: Determine vector directions from charge signs (like charges repel, opposite attract).

common_misconceptions.text: Substituting negative signs of charges into vector magnitude formulas and treating a negative F as a vector direction without a diagram.
common_misconceptions.correction: Always compute magnitude with |q_1 q_2| and draw the force/field vectors explicitly.

subject: Physics
topic: Direct Current (DC) Circuits, Joule's Law and Generators
subtopic: Resistivity, Series/Parallel Resistors, Joule Heating, EMF & Efficiency
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Physics Electricity Unit 2: Direct Current, Joule's Law, and Generators/Motors (ចរន្តអគ្គិសនីជាប់ ច្បាប់ស៊ូល និងជនិតា). Wire resistance is R = rho L / S. Joule's Law gives thermal heat dissipated in a resistor: Q = R I^2 t. A generator with EMF E and internal resistance r delivers terminal voltage U = E - Ir, total power P_total = E I, useful external power P_ext = U I, and circuit efficiency eta = U / E = R / (R + r).

source.section: Resistivity, Series/Parallel Resistors, Joule Heating, EMF & Efficiency

metadata.topic_khmer: សៀគ្វីចរន្តជាប់ ច្បាប់ស៊ូល និងជនិតាអគ្គិសនី
metadata.subtopic_khmer: រេស៊ីស្ទីវីតេ បង្គុំរេស៊ីស្តង់ ច្បាប់ស៊ូល-ឡិន កម្លាំងអគ្គិចលករ និងទិន្នផលសៀគ្វី
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាចរន្តអគ្គិសនីជាប់ រេស៊ីស្តង់នៃខ្សែចម្លង R = ρL/S បង្គុំរេស៊ីស្តង់ ច្បាប់ស៊ូល Q = RI²t ច្បាប់អូមចំពោះជនិតា និងគ្រឿងទទួល ព្រមទាំងទិន្នផលសៀគ្វីអគ្គិសនី។
metadata.starter_problem: \mathcal{E} = 12\text{ V}, \; r = 1\,\Omega, \; R = 5\,\Omega. \text{ Find current } I, \text{ voltage } U, \text{ and power } P.
learning_objectives: Calculate wire resistance R = rho L / S and equivalent resistance of series-parallel combinations
Compute electrical energy W = UIt, Joule heat Q = R I^2 t, and electrical power P = UI
Apply Ohm's Law for generators (U = E - Ir) and receivers/motors (U = E' + Ir') and calculate circuit efficiency

concepts.title: Joule's Law & Electrical Power (ច្បាប់ស៊ូល និងអានុភាពអគ្គិសនី)
concepts.summary: Thermal energy Q = R I^2 t and power P = U I.
concepts.body: When current I flows through resistance R for time t, electrical energy is converted into heat according to Joule's Law: Q = R I^2 t = U I t = (U^2 / R) t (in Joules).

concepts.title: Generators, Receivers & Complete Circuit Efficiency (ជនិតា គ្រឿងទទួល និងទិន្នផល)
concepts.summary: Terminal voltage U = E - Ir and efficiency eta = U / E = R / (R + r).
concepts.body: For a generator of EMF E and internal resistance r connected to external resistor R, I = E / (R + r), U = E - Ir = IR, and efficiency is eta = P_useful / P_total = U / E = R / (R + r).

prerequisites: Electric charge and current I = Q/t

formulas.name: Wire Resistance, Joule's Law & Circuit Efficiency
formulas.expression: R = \rho\frac{L}{S}, \quad Q = RI^2 t, \quad I = \frac{\mathcal{E}}{R + r}, \quad \eta = \frac{U}{\mathcal{E}} = \frac{R}{R + r}

examples.problem: A generator with E = 12 V and r = 1 Ohm supplies an external resistor R = 5 Ohm for t = 10 minutes. Find the current I, terminal voltage U, efficiency eta, and heat generated in R.
solution_steps: Step 2: Efficiency eta = U / E = 10 / 12 = 83.3%.
Step 3: Convert t = 10 min = 600 s. Heat in R: Q = R I^2 t = 5 * 4 * 600 = 12000 J.

exercises.prompt: An electric heater rated at 220 V, 1100 W operates for 30 minutes. Find the current drawn and total energy consumed in kJ.
hints: Use I = P / U and W = P * t (with t = 1800 s).

solution_steps: Step 1: Reduce external resistor networks to a single equivalent resistance R_eq.
Step 2: Apply I = E / (R_eq + r) to find main current.
Step 3: Work backward to find branch voltages, currents, and Joule heat (with time in seconds).

common_misconceptions.text: Assuming terminal voltage U of a real battery is always equal to its EMF E.
common_misconceptions.correction: When current I > 0 is drawn, internal resistance drops voltage rI, so U = E - Ir < E.

subject: Physics
topic: Geometrical Optics: Refraction, Snell's Law and Thin Lenses
subtopic: Snell-Descartes Law, Total Internal Reflection, Thin Lens Formula & Magnification
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Physics Optics Unit: Geometrical Optics (អុបទិចធរណីមាត្រ). Refractive index is n = c/v >= 1. Snell-Descartes Law of Refraction states n_1 sin(theta_1) = n_2 sin(theta_2). When light travels from a denser medium (n_1) to a less dense medium (n_2 < n_1), total internal reflection (ចំណាំងផ្លាតទាំងស្រុង) occurs when theta_1 > theta_c where sin(theta_c) = n_2 / n_1. For spherical mirrors and thin lenses (ឡង់ទីស្តើង), the conjugate equation is 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i, optical power is D = 1/f (in diopters, m^{-1}), and linear magnification is gamma = -d_i / d_o = h_i / h_o.

concepts.title: Snell-Descartes Law & Total Internal Reflection (ច្បាប់ដេកាត និងចំណាំងផ្លាតទាំងស្រុង)
concepts.summary: n_1 sin(i_1) = n_2 sin(i_2) and critical angle sin(i_c) = n_2 / n_1.
concepts.body: Angles of incidence and refraction are always measured from the normal to the surface. When n_1 > n_2, the critical angle i_c satisfies sin(i_c) = n_2 / n_1; for any angle of incidence i_1 > i_c, 100% of the light is reflected back into medium 1.

concepts.title: Thin Lenses & Sign Conventions (ឡង់ទីស្តើង និងសញ្ញាសន្មត)
concepts.body: Sign conventions: f > 0 for a converging lens, f < 0 for a diverging lens; d_o > 0 for a real object; d_i > 0 for a real image (inverted, gamma < 0) and d_i < 0 for a virtual image (upright, gamma > 0). Optical power in diopters (dp) is D = 1/f with f in meters.

examples.problem: Areal object is placed d_o = 30 cm in front of a converging lens of focal length f = +20 cm. Find the image position d_i, magnification gamma, and nature of the image.
solution_steps: Step 2: Since d_i > 0, the image is real.
Step 3: Magnification gamma = -d_i / d_o = -60 / 30 = -2 (inverted and twice as tall).

examples.problem: A light ray travels from air (n_1 = 1.0) into glass (n_2 = 1.5) at an angle of incidence theta_1 = 30 degrees. Find sin(theta_2) and the critical angle for glass-to-air.
solution_steps: Step 1: 1.0 * sin(30 deg) = 1.5 * sin(theta_2) => 0.5 = 1.5 sin(theta_2) => sin(theta_2) = 1/3.
Step 2: Critical angle from glass to air: sin(theta_c) = 1.0 / 1.5 = 2/3.

exercises.prompt: A diverging lens has focal length f = -20 cm. An object is placed at d_o = 20 cm. Find the image distance d_i and magnification gamma.
exercises.answer: d_i = -10 cm, gamma = +0.5 (virtual, upright, half size)

solution_steps: Step 1: Always measure optical angles from the normal to the interface, not from the surface.
Step 2: Assign the correct sign to f (+ for converging, - for diverging) before using 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i.

common_misconceptions.text: Using the angle between the ray and the mirror/glass surface instead of the angle with the normal.
common_misconceptions.correction: If a ray makes angle alpha with the surface, its angle of incidence with the normal is theta_1 = 90 deg - alpha.
